title: The Pirate Ship
seo_title: Pirate Ship Charcuterie Board: Bread Galleon & Shopping List
description: A pirate ship charcuterie board for 12 to 15: a sourdough galleon with prosciutto sails and breadstick masts, carrying salami cargo past a brie treasure island.
hook: A bread galleon in full sail, loaded with salami cargo and sailing past a treasure island of brie.
why: The hull is a long loaf of sourdough, hollowed and filled with cargo, so the shape is sturdy before you add a single slice. Thick breadsticks are the masts and draped prosciutto slices are the sails.

Mozzarella balls make the cannonballs, a whole brie becomes the treasure island, and Gouda, cheddar and salami fill the sea around it. It's made for kids' birthdays and anyone who likes a board with a story.

timeline.what: Hollow the bread hull (wrap it in plastic), roll the mozzarella cannonballs, and cut the pepper flags.
Fill the hull and rig the masts and sails.
Lay the sea, then the treasure island and the shores.
Add the gold coins and the rope.

faq.q: How do you make a pirate ship charcuterie board?
faq.a: Hollow a long sourdough loaf for the hull, stand breadsticks in it as masts, drape prosciutto as sails and fill it with salami and cheese. The book has the full steps.

faq.q: What size loaf do I need?
faq.a: A sourdough bâtard about 16 inches long.

Hollow the loaf and cube the cheese the day before; keep the loaf wrapped so it doesn't dry out. Keep meat, cheese and cut fruit out no more than 2 hours, or 1 hour above 90°F. For a long party, build half, keep the refill in the fridge and top it up halfway through.
